_about: Public-domain William Laud (1573-1645), Archbishop of Canterbury, for the Word Hoard: his Works in the Library of Anglo-Catholic Theology (Oxford: J. H. Parker, 1847-1860, seven volumes in nine: sermons, the Conference with Fisher, devotions and diary, history of his troubles and trial, the Chancellorship of Oxford, letters, notes on Bellarmine), from Internet Archive scans. Laud is the high-church archbishop whose policies the Puritans and Covenanters resisted; he is shelved as part of the record. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 40 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

_alternates.laud-copies: Other scans of the LACT Works (Toronto Robarts, Illinois, Google and Princeton copies); the separate Oxford printings of the Private Devotions (1838), the Conference with Fisher (1839), the three speeches (1840) and the Sermons (1829), all contained in the Works; his 1621-1628 sermons and 1637 Star-Chamber speech in first printings (EEBO)

_excluded.laud-other: The 1637 Scottish Book of Common Prayer (a liturgy of the Church of Scotland, not his work); Original Letters on his benefactions (1841, documents by others); biographies
